title: A prospective feasibility study on smartphone-based wide-field fundus documentation in screening for retinopathy of prematurity
summary:
Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is an eye disease that can occur in babies born very early or very small and, if left untreated, can lead to blindness. For this reason, the retina of these babies is examined regularly. Until now, the findings have usually only been sketched by hand or photographed with very expensive special cameras.

In this study, we investigate whether an ordinary smartphone can be used during the normal eye examination to record a short video of the retina, from which software then automatically creates a stitched wide-field image ("collage") of the retina. This could make it possible to document the findings objectively and, for example, share them with specialists — without expensive equipment and without extra burden for the child, since only the video is added.

Participants are, on the one hand, preterm infants during their routine screening examination and, on the other hand, adult volunteers whose recordings help to test the software under simpler conditions. We mainly look at how reliably usable retinal images can be produced from the videos.

interventions.name:
Preterm infants with a guideline indication for ROP screening. After the clinical examination with binocular indirect ophthalmoscopy, a short fundus video is recorded with a smartphone (4K), once per eye.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Group A (preterm infants)
Preterm infants with an indication for ROP screening according to the German S2k guideline DOG/BVA 024-010.
Circulatory and respiratory status sufficiently stable for a regular ROP screening examination at the planned time point (as decided by the attending neonatologist).
Written informed consent of the legal guardians.

Group B (adults)

Age ≥ 18 years.
Clear optical media, adequate pupillary dilation under mydriasis.
Written informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Group A (preterm infants)
Acute cardiorespiratory instability precluding a standard ROP examination at the planned time point.
Pre-existing relevant ocular conditions unrelated to the ROP question that preclude fundus photography (e.g., pronounced tunica vasculosa lentis, corneal opacity, congenital cataract).
Lack of consent of the legal guardians to processing of the video recording.

Group B (adults)
Contraindication to mydriasis (e.g., known narrow anterior chamber angle, angle-closure glaucoma).
Pregnancy or breastfeeding.
Relevant media opacities, silicone-oil or gas tamponade, retinal detachment > 1 quadrant.
Increased photosensitivity that impedes the retinal examination.
Lack of consent.
